what_happened: Reconstructed the exact end-to-end mechanism for task #467's historical scope-excursion drop by matching the issue's zero-phase/zero-dispatch-seq shape and exact timestamp against git-commit-scoped.sh's own internal V10 issue-record call (not WORK(h)/(i) or git-commit-phase.sh's self-check, which have distinct message text) and against the task-creation commit's timestamp, establishing that no staging-side fix is needed -- only the Containment allowlist itself is defective.

Research report pinned exact edit points (git-commit-scoped.sh:499, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1670, git-commit-phase.sh's absent Site 2 allowlist) and settled both the consolidation verdict and the membership list, so planning only had to verify them by direct read rather than re-derive; all three were confirmed accurate. Plan validated with 0 warnings on first pass.

Research recommended sourcing the shared library at all three sites but did not specify the source-failure fallback. A defensive 'source ... 2>/dev/null' that silently yields nothing would EMPTY the splice and regress today's admission of specs/TODO.md and specs/state.json at Sites 1 and 3 -- a narrower scope than before the fix. Plan adds Decision 2: fall back to the hardcoded two-literal pair on any source/function failure, pinned by a Site 3 fixture (Z18).
